mainTopic: Liability for offering מזבח items outside the עזרה, and how much קטורת counts as a real הקטרה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא of רבי יהושע about how much of an animal offering must remain for its blood to be sprinkled. A כזית of meat or of חלב is enough, but half-and-half does not combine, except by an עולה. A מנחה never counts, and רב פפא explains this means the מנחת נסכים that comes with the animal. Then a new משנה teaches that offering even a כזית of the קומץ, לבונה, קטורת or certain מנחות outside the עזרה makes a person חייב. רבי אליעזר disagrees and requires the whole item. The משנה adds that an item missing even a little brings no liability, and that offering meat together with אימורים outside does. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that burning half a פרס of קטורת inside leaves the community פטור, meaning it has fulfilled its obligation. רבי זירא asks how רבי אליעזר could agree to this. רבה, אביי and רבא each try to explain where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים really argue, and the first two answers are rejected. רבא's own answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A כזית of fat is enough, but half meat and half fat is not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי יהושע continues. If a כזית of חלב remains, the blood is sprinkled. If only half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of חלב remain, the blood is not sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if an olive-bulk of fat remains, he sprinkles the blood. If half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat remain, he does not sprinkle the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting just before. The ברייתא explains how much of an animal offering must survive for its blood to still be sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full כזית of meat, or a full כזית of חלב, is enough to allow זריקת הדם. But two halves from different parts do not add up. The meat is meant to be eaten and the חלב is meant to be burned on the מזבח, so they have different jobs.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, the minimum amount that counts in many halachos
The fats of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
The meat of the offering, which is eaten
He sprinkles the blood on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new teaching. It is the middle of רבי יהושע's ברייתא, which began with 'if a כזית of meat remains.'

phrases.english: Or an olive-bulk of fat – he sprinkles the blood.

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב –
phrases.english: Half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat –
he does not sprinkle the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי יהושע quoted just before this section
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבי יהושע about how much of an offering must remain for זריקה

steps.title: By an עולה the halves combine, but a מנחה never counts
steps.stepSummary: By an עולה, half a כזית of meat plus half a כזית of חלב is enough, because the whole animal is burned. A מנחה, even if all of it remains, does not allow זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by a burnt offering, half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat is enough to sprinkle the blood, because all of it is burned completely. And a meal offering, even if all of it still exists, he does not sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives an exception for an עולה and then adds a ruling about a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By an עולה, the meat and the חלב have the same job, since everything is burned on the מזבח, so the two halves can join together. The last line says that a מנחה, even if it is complete, cannot be the leftover that allows זריקה. This line sounds strange, because a מנחה has no blood, so the גמרא asks about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Completely burned
A meal offering made of flour
Still exists, intact

steps.whatToRemember: Different parts of an offering only combine to a כזית if they share the same purpose. By an עולה, everything is burned, so they combine.

phrases.english: But with a burnt offering, half an olive-bulk of meat

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב – זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם,
phrases.english: and half an olive-bulk of fat – he sprinkles the blood,
because all of it is completely burned.
And a meal offering, even if all of it still exists –
he should not sprinkle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְעוֹלָה, חֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the exception of an עולה and a ruling about a מנחה to the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By an עולה, half meat and half fat combine to allow זריקה. A מנחה, even if whole, does not allow זריקה.

steps.title: What does a meal offering have to do with sprinkling blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא mentions a מנחה at all, since a מנחה has no blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A meal offering, what is its relevance here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question the last line of the ברייתא. This question sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה is made of flour and has no blood to sprinkle. So the ruling 'he should not sprinkle' seems to make no sense for a מנחה. The גמרא wants to know what case the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its business here? What is it doing in this discussion?

phrases.english: A meal offering – what is its relevance?
phrases.notes: Literally 'what is its work?' The point is that a מנחה has no blood, so why mention it here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the final clause of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מנחה the ברייתא means, given that a מנחה has no blood

steps.title: It means the מנחת נסכים that comes with an animal offering
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא is talking about the מנחת נסכים brought together with an animal זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it means the meal offering of libations that comes with the animal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The ברייתא's מנחה is the one that comes along with an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal itself was lost but its accompanying מנחה is still whole, you might think that counts as a leftover of the offering. The ברייתא teaches that it does not, so the blood may not be sprinkled. Only meat or חלב of the animal itself counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering brought with an animal offering, along with its wine
An animal offering

steps.whatToRemember: The accompanying מנחת נסכים is not part of the animal, so it can never be the leftover that allows זריקת הדם.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The meal offering of libations that comes with the animal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא מִנְחַת נְסָכִים הַבָּאָה עִם הַזֶּבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא refers to the מנחת נסכים that accompanies an animal זבח, which does not count as a leftover of the animal.

steps.title: New משנה: offering a כזית of these items outside makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the קומץ, לבונה, קטורת, מנחת כהנים, מנחת כהן משיח, and מנחת נסכים. Offering even a כזית of any one of them outside the עזרה makes a person חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The handful, the frankincense, the incense, the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest, and the meal offering of libations: if one offered an olive-bulk from any one of them outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that burning just a כזית of these מזבח items outside the בית המקדש is enough to make a person חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these items are supposed to be burned on the מזבח. According to this first opinion, burning a כזית outside counts as a real offering outside, even if he did not burn the whole thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Frankincense
The incense
The daily meal offering of the כהן גדול
Outside the עזרה

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The handful, the frankincense, the incense,
the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and the meal offering of libations,
where one offered an olive-bulk from one of them outside –
he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering a כזית of any of these מזבח items outside makes one חייב.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: not liable unless he offers all of it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees and exempts the person unless he offers the entire item outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר exempts him, until he offers all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר argues on the first opinion in the משנה. For him, a כזית is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says a כזית counts as an offering outside. רבי אליעזר holds that only offering the whole item outside makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, rules not liable
All of them, the whole amount

steps.confusionAlert: 'All of them' does not mean all six items together. It means the whole of whichever item he offered.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer exempts,
until he offers all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One is חייב only if he offers the whole item outside.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: offering the leftover כזית outside makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: If he offered most of the item inside and left over a כזית, then offered that כזית outside, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them, if he offered them inside and left over an olive-bulk from them, and offered it outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case where even רבי אליעזר agrees the person is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the כזית is not part of a whole item. It is all that was left after the rest was properly offered inside. In this case the person is חייב for offering it outside, even according to רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside the עזרה
Left over

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about offering a כזית of a whole item outside. When only a כזית is left and he offers it outside, he is חייב according to everyone.

phrases.english: And all of them that he offered inside
and left over an olive-bulk from them,
and offered it outside – he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁהִקְרִיב בִּפְנִים וְשִׁיֵּיר מֵהֶן כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where רבי אליעזר agrees there is liability
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering the leftover כזית outside, after the rest was offered inside, makes one חייב.

steps.title: An item that is missing even a little brings no liability outside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if any of the listed items was short even a tiny amount, offering it outside makes a person פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If any of these items was missing even the smallest amount, and he offered it outside, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list from before. It says that if the קומץ, לבונה, קטורת, or any of the listed מנחות was missing even a tiny bit, offering it outside brings no punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said even a כזית offered outside makes a person חייב. Now it adds a limit: if the whole item was incomplete from the start, he is פטור. The point seems to be that an incomplete item is not a proper offering, so offering it outside is not counted.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them, meaning all the items listed earlier
Were lacking, were missing some of their amount
Any amount at all, even the tiniest bit
Exempt, not punished

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 7. There, he offered most of the item inside and then offered the leftover כזית outside, and he is חייב. Here, the whole item was short from the start, so offering it outside makes him פטור.

phrases.english: And all of them that were lacking any amount at all,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the items listed in step 5: קומץ, לבונה, קטורת, and the מנחות.

phrases.english: and he offered it outside, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the rule of liability for a כזית: an item that was incomplete from the start brings no liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any of the listed items that was short even a tiny amount, if offered outside, brings no liability.

steps.title: Offering meat together with the altar portions outside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one who offers קדשים and אימורים outside the עזרה is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who offers sacrificial meat and the altar portions outside is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: someone offered sacrificial meat together with the parts meant for the מזבח, outside the עזרה. He is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of a קרבן is meant to be eaten, not burned, so offering it does not by itself create liability. The אימורים are the parts that go on the מזבח, and offering those outside is what makes him חייב. Mixing the meat in does not cancel the liability for the אימורים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers, one who brings up as a קרבן
Here: the sacrificial meat that is meant to be eaten
The parts of an animal קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
Liable, punishable

phrases.english: One who offers sacrificial meat and the altar portions
outside the courtyard is liable.
phrases.notes: He is liable because of the אימורים; the meat itself, which is for eating, does not make him liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the משנה's list of rules about offering outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering meat together with אימורים outside makes a person חייב, because of the אימורים.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with two rules: an item missing even a tiny amount brings no liability outside, and offering meat with אימורים outside does bring liability.

steps.title: A ברייתא about burning קטורת outside and inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: burning a כזית of קטורת outside makes a person חייב, while burning half a פרס inside makes him פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins. The Rabbis taught: One who burns an olive-bulk of incense outside is liable. If he burns half a פרס inside, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting a ברייתא with two rules about קטורת. The rest of the discussion is built on the second rule, about half a פרס inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daily קטורת offered inside is a full פרס each morning and each afternoon. The first rule says that outside, even a small כזית is enough to make a person חייב. The second rule says burning only half a פרס inside makes him פטור, and the גמרא will now ask what 'exempt' means there.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
One who burns something as an offering
Half a מנה; the amount of קטורת burned each morning and each afternoon
Inside the בית המקדש

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
One who burns an olive-bulk of incense outside is liable.
If he burns half a peras inside, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: A full פרס of קטורת is burned inside each morning and each afternoon, so half a פרס is only half of the proper amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּקְטִיר כְּזַיִת בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its discussion with a ברייתא related to the משנה's rule about a כזית of קטורת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning a כזית of קטורת outside makes a person חייב; burning half a פרס inside makes him פטור.

steps.title: Assuming 'exempt' means a non-priest is exempt, and challenging it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes that 'exempt' in the ברייתא means a זר who burned half a פרס inside is exempt, then challenges this: it is a real act of הקטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We first assume: what does 'exempt' mean? A non-priest is exempt. But why should he be exempt? It is an act of burning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a first reading of the word 'exempt': a זר who burned half a פרס inside is not punished. Then it attacks that reading right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זר who performs a service in the בית המקדש is normally punished. The first rule of the ברייתא shows that even a כזית counts as a real act of burning, so half a פרס should surely count too. That makes it hard to say the זר is exempt, and the גמרא will need a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters our mind; we would first assume
A non-כהן, who may not do the services in the בית המקדש
Why?
An act of burning an offering

phrases.english: It enters our mind to say:
What is 'exempt'? A non-priest is exempt;
Why should he be? It is an act of burning!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין: מַאי פָּטוּר – פָּטוּר זָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the second rule of the ברייתא from step 10 and challenges the first reading of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'exempt' in the ברייתא means a זר who burned half a פרס inside is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own first rule shows that even a כזית counts as a real act of burning. So a זר burning half a פרס inside has done a real הקטרה and should be punished, not exempt.

steps.title: Exempt means the community has fulfilled its obligation
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'exempt' in the ברייתא does not refer to a זר. It means the community is exempt: burning half a פרס inside still counts for the community's incense obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said that רב חסדא said that רב ירמיה בר אבא said that רב said: What does 'exempt' mean? The community is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last step. It reads the word 'exempt' in a completely different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading said a זר who burned half a פרס inside is exempt from punishment, but that did not work because it is a real burning. רב says 'exempt' means the community has done its duty, even though less than the full amount was burned.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (what does it mean)
Exempt / free of obligation
The community (the public obligation of the daily incense)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Chisda said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
What does 'exempt' mean? The community is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 11 by reinterpreting 'exempt'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Exempt' meant a זר who burned half a פרס inside is not punished.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Exempt' means the community fulfills its incense obligation with half a פרס.

steps.title: How can רבי אליעזר agree to this?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא is troubled by רב's added comment that even רבי אליעזר agrees. רבי אליעזר holds that burning a small amount is not a real הקטרה, so how could he say the community fulfills its duty with less than a פרס?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: If anything is hard for me, this is hard for me. רב said about this ברייתא that on this point even רבי אליעזר agrees. But רבי אליעזר says it is not a real act of burning!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא raises a difficulty against another statement of רב about the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the ruling that the community fulfills its duty with less than a פרס is agreed even by רבי אליעזר. But רבי אליעזר treats a small amount of incense as not a real הקטרה, since he exempts one who burns it outside. If it is not a real burning, it should not count for the community either.

keyTerms.meaning: If something is difficult for me
Agrees / concedes
A sacrificial act of burning

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי – הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי:
phrases.english: If something is difficult for me, this is difficult for me:
That which Rav said about it:
phrases.notes: 'About it' means about this same ברייתא of half a פרס.

phrases.english: In this, even Rabbi Eliezer agrees;
for Rabbi Eliezer
is saying that it is not an act of burning!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי – הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's further claim that רבי אליעזר also accepts the ruling of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that even רבי אליעזר agrees that less than a פרס satisfies the community
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר holds that a small amount is not a real הקטרה, since he exempts it outside. So it should not satisfy the community's obligation either.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about the incense of the היכל
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that for the daily incense burned in the היכל, everyone agrees, including רבי אליעזר. A small amount counts there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Regarding the burning in the היכל, everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins answering רבי זירא's difficulty. He limits where רבי אליעזר's view applies, and the next step finishes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about the daily incense in the היכל, and there no one argues: a small amount is a real הקטרה. So רב can say that even רבי אליעזר agrees with the ברייתא, and רבי אליעזר's disagreement must be about a different incense.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, where the golden altar stood
Everyone (all opinions)
They do not disagree

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Regarding the burning of the Sanctuary,
phrases.notes: This is the daily incense burned on the golden altar.

phrases.english: everyone does not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהַקְטָרָה דְּהֵיכָל – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by separating types of incense.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the dispute to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's view that a small amount is not a real הקטרה applies to all incense.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the היכל incense, everyone, including רבי אליעזר, agrees that a small amount counts.

steps.title: The argument is about the inner incense and 'his handful'
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue only about the inner incense of יום כיפור. One side holds 'מלא חפניו' is an exact measure, and the other holds it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is about the inner burning. One holds that 'his handful' is exact, and the other holds that 'his handful' is not exact.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his answer by showing exactly where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים do argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the incense brought inside on יום כיפור, the תורה says 'מלא חפניו'. רבי אליעזר reads this as an exact measure, so less than that is not a real הקטרה and burning it outside is exempt. The חכמים do not read it as exact, so even a small amount counts and burning it outside makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside: here, the קודש הקדשים on יום כיפור
His full handful
Exactly / precisely as stated
One master holds

steps.whatToRemember: There is no argument about the daily היכל incense: a small amount counts. רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue only about the יום כיפור inner incense, depending on whether 'מלא חפניו' is exact.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is about the inner burning;
phrases.notes: This is the incense brought into the קודש הקדשים on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: for one master holds: 'his full handful' is exact,
and the other master holds: 'his full handful' is not exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's answer begun in step 14 by locating the real dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Locating the dispute in a different case, based on how a פסוק is read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר disagrees about every kind of incense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is only about the inner יום כיפור incense: is 'מלא חפניו' an exact measure or not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבה, רב's statement holds: even רבי אליעזר agrees that a small amount of היכל incense counts, and his disagreement concerns only the inner incense. אביי challenges this in the next step.

steps.title: אביי objects: the word 'statute' is written about the inner incense
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: the word 'חוקה' is written about the יום כיפור service, including the inner burning of incense. So 'מלא חפניו' must be an exact measure, and nobody can argue about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But the word 'חוקה' is written exactly about the burning of incense inside!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's explanation from Step 15. רבה said רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about whether 'מלא חפניו' is exact. אביי says that cannot be a real argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תורה uses the word 'חוקה' for a service, every detail must be done exactly as written. The word 'חוקה' is written about the יום כיפור service, which includes the inner incense. So 'מלא חפניו' has to be exact, and there is no room for the dispute רבה described.

keyTerms.meaning: Statute: a word that tells us every detail of a service is required
Burning (of incense or offerings)
Inside: here, the קודש הקדשים on יום כיפור
But look! (opens an objection)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבה, who gave the explanation in the last step.

phrases.english: But when 'statute' is written,
it is written about the burning of the inner incense!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא כִּי קָא כְתִיבָא ״חֻקָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's explanation of the dispute in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue whether 'מלא חפניו' is an exact measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'חוקה' makes every detail required, and it is written about the inner incense, so the handful must be exact according to everyone

steps.title: אביי's new approach: everyone agrees about burning inside
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives his own explanation. When the incense is burned inside on יום כיפור, everyone agrees a full handful is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: About burning inside, everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops רבה's approach and starts his own explanation. First he says what everyone agrees on, which sets up the next step, where he will say what they do argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of 'חוקה', burning the inner incense inside needs a full handful according to everyone. So the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים has to be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier answer and offers a new one
Everyone (all opinions)
They do not argue

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
About burning inside,
phrases.notes: He means burning the יום כיפור incense in the קודש הקדשים, where it belongs.

phrases.english: everyone agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's explanation after אביי's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of the dispute that moves it to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about whether a handful is needed for the inner service itself
steps.terutzMaskana: Inside, everyone requires a full handful; the dispute must be elsewhere

steps.title: The real dispute: burning the inner incense outside
steps.stepSummary: אביי says they argue about someone who burns the inner incense outside. One side learns its measure from the regular incense (so a כזית makes him liable), and the other side does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is about burning outside. One master holds we learn the inner from the outer, and the other master holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his explanation by saying what the argument is really about: the measure that makes a person liable for burning the inner incense outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the regular incense of the היכל outside makes a person liable for a כזית. The חכמים learn the inner incense from it, so a כזית is enough for liability. רבי אליעזר does not learn one from the other, so a person is liable only for a full handful, the amount needed inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside: here, outside the Temple courtyard. It is also used for the outer incense of the היכל
We learn (derive) one case from another
One master holds

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'חוץ' is used in two ways in this step. 'הקטרה דחוץ' means burning outside the courtyard. In 'פנים מחוץ', 'חוץ' means the outer incense of the היכל.

phrases.english: Where they argue is about burning outside;
one master holds: we learn the inner from the outer,
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים: the inner incense gets the regular incense's measure of a כזית.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: we do not learn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's new explanation by naming the case they argue about
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the dispute in a new case: liability for burning outside
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים learn the inner incense from the outer (a כזית makes him liable); רבי אליעזר does not (only a handful makes him liable)
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole argument. It is no longer about how to do the יום כיפור service itself. It is about the measure for the sin of burning outside.

steps.title: רבא: the רבנן do not even learn outer from outer
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's explanation. The רבנן do not even learn other outer services from the outer incense. So they surely would not learn the inner incense from the outer incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now, if the רבנן do not learn outer from outer, is it even a question whether they would learn inner from outer?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanation אביי just gave for the חכמים' opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the רבנן learn the inner incense from the outer incense. But רבא points out that the רבנן do not even learn from the outer incense to other outer services, which are much more similar to it. If they refuse the easier comparison, they would certainly refuse the harder one.

keyTerms.meaning: Now: opens a 'how much more so' argument
The Rabbis (the חכמים)
Is it even needed / is it even a question?

steps.whatToRemember: אביי moved the dispute to burning the inner incense outside: the חכמים learn inner from outer, and רבי אליעזר does not. רבא pushes back that the רבנן do not even learn outer from outer, so they would surely not learn inner from outer.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא חוּץ מֵחוּץ לָא יָלְפִי רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Now, outer from outer the Rabbis do not learn,
is it even a question about inner from outer?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַשְׁתָּא חוּץ מֵחוּץ לָא יָלְפִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation אביי gave for the רבנן in Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the רבנן learn the inner incense from the outer incense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if they will not compare two outer cases, they surely will not compare an inner case to an outer one

steps.title: Which source is רבא pointing to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching shows that the רבנן do not learn one outer service from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about רבא's last statement: what source was he pointing to? This sets up the next step, where the source is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רבא said the רבנן do not even learn outer services from the outer incense. That claim needs a source. Here the גמרא asks for it before checking whether רבא's challenge holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking which teaching is meant)

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He means: what is the teaching רבא had in mind when he said the רבנן don't learn outer from outer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבא's challenge in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which source shows that the רבנן do not learn the measure of one outer service from another outer service.

steps.title: The ברייתא: no liability for an incomplete offering outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who offers less than a full measure outside the עזרה is not liable, because the פסוק says 'לעשות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: You might think that someone who offers up outside less than a כזית of the קומץ, or less than a כזית of the אימורין, or who pours less than three לוגין of wine or less than three לוגין of water, is liable. So the פסוק says 'לַעֲשׂוֹת' (to do it): he is liable for a complete offering, but not for an incomplete one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא says you are only liable for offering outside the עזרה when you offer the full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לעשות' teaches that liability needs the complete service. Below a כזית of קומץ or אימורין there is no liability. For wine or water libations, the measure is three לוגין, so anything less brings no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
The parts of an animal offering that are burned on the מזבח
Someone who pours a libation (wine or water) on the מזבח
A liquid measure; three לוגין is the full libation here
The פסוק comes to teach
Complete / incomplete

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: You might think that one who offers up
less than an olive-size of the handful
or less than an olive-size of the sacrificial parts,
or one who pours less than three לוגין of wine
[or less] than three לוגין of water –
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets isn't in every version, but it belongs here. Water was poured on the מזבח on סוכות.

phrases.english: would be liable?
The פסוק says: 'to do it' –
for the complete one he is liable,
but he is not liable for the incomplete one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by quoting the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא that requires a complete measure for liability when offering outside, including three full לוגין for libations.

steps.title: Proof: the רבנן do not learn outer from outer
steps.stepSummary: Less than three לוגין of wine still holds many olive-sizes, yet there is no liability. So the רבנן do not learn the libation's measure from the outer incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: But less than three לוגין contains many olive-sizes, and still he is not liable. So the רבנן do not learn an outer service from an outer service!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows how the ברייתא proves רבא's point. A libation of less than three לוגין is much more than a כזית, yet it brings no liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן learned the libation's measure from the outer incense, where a כזית is enough, then a few olive-sizes of wine would make him liable. Since he is not liable, they do not learn one outer service from another. So they surely would not learn the inner incense from the outer incense, and אביי's explanation falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Several olive-sizes
They learn (one law from another)
An outer service from an outer service

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן require a full measure for each service offered outside. They do not borrow the outer incense's כזית for other services, so אביי's explanation (step 18) does not work.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חוץ' here does not mean outside the עזרה. It means the outer services: the regular היכל incense and services like the libations, as opposed to the inner incense of יום כיפור.

phrases.english: But look: less than three לוגין,
which contain several olive-sizes –
and the רבנן do not learn outer from outer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 21 to support רבא's challenge in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the רבנן do not learn the measure of one outer service from the outer incense.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that less than three לוגין of wine brings no liability, even though it holds many olive-sizes.

steps.title: רבא begins a new explanation: two half-פרס portions
steps.stepSummary: Since אביי's explanation fell, רבא offers his own: the case is someone who set aside the incense as two half-פרס portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: For example, where he set them aside as two half-פרס portions...
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי's explanation was rejected, רבא now starts his own explanation of the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים. His sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows that the earlier explanations are dropped and a new one begins. רבא places the argument in a specific case, where the incense was set aside as two halves of a פרס rather than as one whole portion. The details of how this case explains the argument come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier answer for a new one)
He set them aside (designated them)
Halves of a פרס, a fixed portion of incense

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
for example, where he set them aside as two half-פרס portions

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected explanation with a new one from רבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument is about learning the inner incense's measure from the outer incense (אביי), and that has been disproved.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about a case where the incense was set aside as two half-פרס portions. The details continue next.
